# Guion 004: In This World, Your Shadow Walks Toward Who You Like

Guion original. Sale de la premisa 5 del banco
(`docs/05-guiones-y-fuentes.md`): la sombra te delata en el peor momento. Aquí
el peor momento es una feria al atardecer, y la sombra de ella tiene otros
planes.

- **Tema**: amor (primer gusto, nivel "me gusta" y tomarse de la mano)
- **Final**: cómico con un golpe tierno antes del remate
- **Regla**: tu sombra se levanta y camina hacia quien te gusta, y no la puedes
  llamar de vuelta
- **Costo de la regla**: nadie puede esconder un gusto; al mediodía la sombra
  es diminuta y segura, pero al atardecer mide doce metros (forty feet) y cruza
  cualquier distancia
- **Detalle sembrado**: la sombra del tío lleva parqueada frente a la tienda de
  donas desde 2011 (bloque 2) y Juniper carga una sombrilla amarilla aunque
  haga sol (bloque 3); en el bloque 7 las dos cosas se juntan: las sombras
  también van hacia la comida, y ella no escondía un gusto por otro, escondía
  una sombra enamorada de los nachos
- **Giro**: la sombra de Juniper pasa de largo junto al narrador. No es "ella
  también gustaba de mí": su sombra no decide por ella, y ella elige con la
  mano
- **Conteo real**: 352 palabras (16, 70, 38, 39, 79, 35, 53, 22), contadas con script
- **Título alterno**: The Yellow Umbrella

## Narración

El texto de la narración va en inglés, a ras de margen, listo para pegar en el
generador de voz. También está en
`004-your-shadow-walks-toward-who-you-like.txt`.

**[1. Gancho]**

In this world, your SHADOW walks toward whoever you like, and you can't call it BACK.

**[2. Ejemplos del mundo]**

It just gets up and goes. My brother's shadow followed a lifeguard around for a whole summer. My math teacher's shadow lies across the lunch lady's shoes every day. They both pretend not to notice. It's not only people, either. My uncle's shadow has been parked outside the donut shop since 2011. Noon is safe, because shadows are tiny. Sunset is dangerous. At sunset, your shadow is FORTY feet long.

**[3. El ángulo del narrador]**

Mine likes Juniper Vale. She sits two rows ahead of me in science. She carries a yellow umbrella everywhere, even when it's sunny. Everyone says she's hiding her shadow from somebody. Probably Dax. Dax can do a backflip.

**[4. Crisis]**

Then the school announced the Sunset Fair. Friday. On the soccer field. At six-thirty, when every shadow is forty feet long. Mine would cross the whole field and tap her on the shoulder in front of three hundred people.

**[5. Tres intentos fallidos]**

So I tried to stop it. First, I tied my shadow to my ankle with a jump rope. It dragged me into a trash can. Second, I wore a sombrero the size of a kiddie pool. My shadow turned into a big circle and rolled toward her like a pancake. Third, at the fair, I pointed nine flashlights at myself to erase it. Instead, I got NINE shadows. All nine ran straight to Juniper. One of them was WAVING.

**[6. Cuarto intento]**

Three hundred people stared. So I did the only thing left. I walked across the field, right behind my own shadows. "Yeah. Those are mine. All nine. I LIKE you. Sorry about the waving one."

**[7. Desenlace]**

Juniper closed her umbrella. First time ever. Her shadow stood up, stretched, and walked right past me. It went straight to the nacho stand and hugged the cheese pump. "It's been like that since third grade," she said. "My shadow likes NACHOS. I get to PICK for myself." Then she took my hand.

**[8. Remate]**

We split a large. Dax did a backflip. Nobody looked. Her shadow still lives at the nacho stand. Mine brings it napkins.

# Guion 005: In This Town, Breakups Make It Snow

Guion original. Sale de la premisa 6 del banco
(`docs/05-guiones-y-fuentes.md`): cada ruptura trae nieve, y lleva tres meses
nevando sobre una sola casa. Aquí la casa es la del narrador, y la nieve no es
de quien todos creen: el narrador lo sabe desde el principio y lo esconde.

- **Tema**: amor visto desde afuera (el hermano menor y la exnovia de su
  hermano, que era como una hermana mayor)
- **Final**: emotivo con remate cómico
- **Regla**: cada ruptura hace nevar, pero solo sobre la casa de la persona a
  la que dejaron
- **Costo de la regla**: la nieve no para hasta que de verdad lo superas; no se
  puede fingir ("the sky checks") y todo el pueblo ve quién sigue dolido
- **Detalle sembrado**: "Marisol taught me to skateboard" y "nobody asks the
  little brother" (bloque 3), más la regla "the sky checks" (bloque 2). Se
  cosechan en el bloque 5 (la nube no se deja engañar) y en el 7 (el bordillo
  donde ella le enseñó a patinar)
- **Giro**: el espectador sabe desde el bloque 3 que la nieve es del hermano
  menor (ironía dramática, no sorpresa). El giro es de ella: tiene su propia
  nube diminuta sobre el bordillo donde le enseñó a patinar, y lleva tres
  meses paleándola
- **Conteo real**: 379 palabras (17, 62, 66, 39, 76, 44, 49, 26), contadas con script
- **Título alterno**: The Snow Cloud

## Narración

El texto de la narración va en inglés, a ras de margen, listo para pegar en el
generador de voz. También está en `005-breakups-make-it-snow.txt`.

**[1. Gancho]**

In this town, every breakup makes it SNOW, but only over the house of whoever got dumped.

**[2. Ejemplos del mundo]**

Small breakup, a few flakes. Big breakup, a BLIZZARD. When the mayor's wife left, he got six feet in July. When Mr. Dobbs got dumped by text, it snowed inside his car. Kids here keep sleds by the front door. We root against every couple. And the snow only stops when you're really over it. You can't fake it. The sky CHECKS.

**[3. El ángulo del narrador]**

It has been snowing on my house for three months. My brother Nico got dumped by Marisol in March. Neighbors still bring him soup. But Nico got over her in a week. He's dating Tabitha from the bowling alley. The snow is all on MY side of the roof. See, Marisol taught me to skateboard. She gave me my helmet. And nobody asks the LITTLE BROTHER.

**[4. Crisis]**

Yesterday the roof made a sound like a giant chewing ice. Dad measured nine feet. The city said stop the snow by Saturday, or we move out. Everybody looked at Nico. So I had to get over her. Fast.

**[5. Tres intentos fallidos]**

First, I just said it. "I'm over it." The cloud dropped one snowball on my head. It AIMED. Second, I boxed up everything she gave me. The helmet. The wheels. A birthday card with a skull on it. Three feet fell in one hour. The mailman quit. Third, I tried being mad at her. I wrote a list of everything wrong with Marisol. It had one thing on it. "LEFT." It snowed inside my sock drawer.

**[6. Cuarto intento]**

So I grabbed my board and skated to her house. Eleven blocks. A little trail of snow followed me the whole way. I knocked. Marisol opened the door. And I said the dumbest sentence of my life. "Did you break up with ME, too?"

**[7. Desenlace]**

She didn't answer. She pointed at her driveway. One TINY cloud. Snowing on one spot. The curb where she taught me to ollie. "Three months," she said. "I shovel that curb every morning." We just stood there. Then her little cloud thinned out. Eleven blocks away, so did mine.

**[8. Remate]**

We skate every Saturday now. Our lawn is green again. Nico is still dating Tabitha. I keep a sled by the door. I'm predicting two inches.

159	
160	El texto de la narración va en inglés, a ras de margen, listo para pegar en el
161	generador de voz. También está en `007-everyone-can-see-who-you-miss.txt`.
162	
163	**[1. Gancho]**
164	
165	In this world, everyone can see who you MISS, because their silhouette walks right next to you.
166	
167	**[2. Ejemplos del mundo]**
168	
169	It's gray and see-through, like a person made of fog. My mom's is shaped like my grandma. My gym teacher's is shaped like his own hair in 2009. The more you miss somebody, the sharper it gets. It only goes away when you see them again, in person. So nobody gets to play it cool. My sister told everyone she was "so over" Kyle. Kyle's fog was carrying her backpack.
170	
171	**[3. El ángulo del narrador]**
172	
173	Mine is shaped like Barty Finch. My biggest RIVAL. Three years of war. Spelling bees. One corn-eating contest that sent us both to the nurse. Then he transferred to a school six miles away. Now I win everything. Last week I won the spelling bee with the word "cat." Also, some guy in a fake mustache keeps booing me from the back row. Unrelated.
174	
175	**[4. Crisis]**
176	
177	Two days after he left, foggy Barty showed up beside me. Everyone saw. And yearbook photos are Friday. I am not getting photographed next to my rival. He's getting sharper, too. He has EYEBROWS now.
178	
179	**[5. Tres intentos fallidos]**
180	
181	So I tried to get rid of him. First, I tried missing someone else harder. I stared at pictures of my grandma for two hours. Now I had TWO fogs. They high-fived. Second, I put a wig on him and said he was my cousin. The wig fell straight through. Third, I held auditions for a new rival. Seven kids showed up. The best one lost on purpose and said "good game." DISGUSTING. Foggy Barty got so sharp I could count his freckles. Eleven.
182	
183	**[6. Cuarto intento]**
184	
185	So Thursday I biked six miles to his school. I waited at the gate. When he came out, I just said it. "I win everything now, and it feels like nothing. Nobody else argues right. I MISS you, okay?" My fog POPPED like a bubble.
186	
187	**[7. Desenlace]**
188	
189	Then I noticed. There was nothing next to Barty. NO fog. My stomach dropped. He turned red. He reached into his backpack and pulled out a fake mustache. "You can't miss somebody you see every week," he said. "Also, your spelling is embarrassing." He'd come to every contest. Six miles each way. Just to BOO me.
190	
191	**[8. Remate]**
192	
193	He transferred back on Monday. We're tied, two hundred twelve to two hundred twelve. Nobody walks next to me anymore. Except Barty. He still boos.

272

284	- **Detalle sembrado**: Bram la guarda en el bolsillo de la camisa y lo abotona

297	
298	**[1. Gancho]**
299	
300	In this world, you can LEND your courage to a friend, but you have NONE until they give it back.
301	
302	**[2. Ejemplos del mundo]**
303	
304	It pops out of your chest like a warm orange marble. Your friend presses it to their chest, and it sinks right in. Now they're brave, and you're not. My dad lent his to my uncle for a wedding toast. Dad spent the whole party in the coat closet. Kids at my school rent theirs out. Two dollars a recess.
305	
306	**[3. El ángulo del narrador]**
307	
308	I never lent mine. Then my best friend Bram had to sing at the talent show. Bram is scared of dogs, escalators, and the word "volunteer." So I handed mine over. He dropped it in his shirt pocket and buttoned it. TWICE. He sang. He got a standing ovation.
309	
310	**[4. Crisis]**
311	
312	That was three weeks ago. He never gave it back. Now Bram eats at the loud table by the window, and I'm scared of everything. Stairs. Soup. SOUP is hot, and it moves. And here's the problem. Asking for your courage back takes COURAGE.
313	
314	**[5. Tres intentos fallidos]**
315	
316	So I wrote him a note. Four drafts. Then I got scared of his locker and ate it. I paid my little sister five dollars to ask for me. She asked for his pudding instead. She got it. Then I rented courage from a first grader named Zeb. Two dollars. It was the size of a pea. It was exactly enough to pet one goose. The goose bit me. Zeb cried until I gave it back. He kept the two dollars.
317	
318	**[6. Cuarto intento]**
319	
320	On Friday I walked to Bram's table with NOTHING. My knees knocked so loud that people turned around. I said, "I need it back. I'm scared of stairs. I'm scared of soup. And I'm scared you like this table better than me."
321	
322	**[7. Desenlace]**
323	
324	Bram unbuttoned his pocket. Twice. There it was. Still warm. He never USED it. "I was too scared to put it in," he said. "What if I broke it? So I just sang SCARED." Then why keep it? His ears went red. "It felt like you were up there with me." He looked at my knees. "Wait. You walked over here WITHOUT it?"
325	
326	**[8. Remate]**
327	
328	I pressed it back in. Stairs are just stairs again. Bram still borrows it every Friday. He never uses it. He just buttons it twice. And my uncle never returned Dad's. We slide pizza under the closet door.

399	# Guion 009: In This Town, Apologies Are Paid in Memories
400	
401	Guion original. Sale de la premisa 13 del banco (`docs/05-guiones-y-fuentes.md`):
402	pedir perdón cuesta un recuerdo feliz; entre más grave, más valioso. Antes de
403	producirlo, repite la búsqueda del título en YouTube y reescribe a tu gusto el
404	gancho y el remate (hay alternativas al final).
405	
406	- **Tema**: familia (hermanos)
407	- **Final**: agridulce con remate cómico
408	- **Regla**: decir "sorry" de verdad cuesta un recuerdo feliz, que sale por la
409	  oreja como una foto luminosa y vuela hacia la persona herida, que se queda
410	  con él
411	- **Costo de la regla**: entre peor la falta, mejor el recuerdo que se pierde;
412	  el pueblo cobra el precio justo y no se puede pagar con sustitutos
413	- **Detalle sembrado**: el mejor recuerdo del narrador, la noche del apagón con
414	  el fuerte de cobijas y una sola cuchara (bloque 3). Se cosecha en el bloque 7:
415	  es justo el recuerdo que se va, y todo lo que el narrador contó de esa noche
416	  lo sabe porque su hermana se lo contó después
417	- **Giro**: el narrador ya no recuerda su mejor noche; su hermana ahora la
418	  recuerda dos veces, una como ella y otra como él, y así descubre cuánto la
419	  admiraba
420	- **Conteo real**: 363 palabras (20, 59, 51, 27, 69, 38, 57, 42), contadas con script

426	generador de voz. También está en `009-apologies-are-paid-in-memories.txt`.

428	**[1. Gancho]**
429	
430	In this town, saying sorry costs you one happy MEMORY, and the worse you messed up, the better the memory.
431	
432	**[2. Ejemplos del mundo]**
433	
434	It slides out of your ear like a little glowing photo and flies to the person you hurt. They keep it. Bump someone in the hall, and you lose a pretty good sandwich. My dad backed over Mr. Tuttle's mailbox and lost a whole BEACH TRIP. Now Mr. Tuttle remembers our vacation. He says the hotel was just okay.
435	
436	**[3. El ángulo del narrador]**
437	
438	I'm fourteen, and I've NEVER said sorry. Not once. So I still have every happy memory I ever made. My best one is a blackout when I was seven. Me and my big sister Nell built a blanket fort. We ate a whole tub of melting ice cream with one spoon.
439	
440	**[4. Crisis]**
441	
442	Then Nell started packing for college. I said, "Good. I finally get your room." She hasn't spoken to me in nine days. She leaves Sunday at noon.
443	
444	**[5. Tres intentos fallidos]**
445	
446	So I tried to fix it for free. I said "my bad." "My bad" costs NOTHING. It bounced off her door. I baked her twenty-four apology cookies. I wrote "oops" on every one in frosting. She fed them to the dog. Then I paid our neighbor Gus six dollars to say sorry for me. He lost a memory of a waterslide. Nell felt nothing. Gus wants his waterslide back.
447	
448	**[6. Cuarto intento]**
449	
450	Sunday, 11:52. Her car was packed. I stood in the driveway and said it. "I'm SORRY. I don't want your room. I want YOU in it." My ear got warm. I figured I'd lose my laser tag birthday.
451	
452	**[7. Desenlace]**
453	
454	A little photo slid out. I saw a flashlight. A blanket. ONE spoon. Then it flew into Nell's forehead, and I couldn't tell you what was on it. Nell started crying. She hugged me so hard my shoes left the driveway. I don't REMEMBER that blackout anymore. Everything I told you about the fort, Nell told me.
455	
456	**[8. Remate]**
457	
458	She got my copy. So now she remembers that night TWICE. Once as her. Once as me. She says in my version, she's ten feet tall. She also says I promised her my dessert until I'm thirty. I can't prove I didn't.

# Guion 006: In This Town, Inside Jokes Become Pets

Guion original. Sale de la premisa 9 del banco
(`docs/05-guiones-y-fuentes.md`): cada chiste interno se vuelve mascota y vive
mientras ambos se rían. Aquí el mejor amigo se muda lejos y las mascotas se van
apagando una por una.

- **Tema**: amistad a distancia
- **Final**: agridulce con remate cómico (las catorce mascotas viejas no
  vuelven; nace una nueva, distinta)
- **Regla**: cada chiste interno se convierte en una mascota que vive mientras
  los dos se sigan riendo
- **Costo de la regla**: no se puede fingir (una risa falsa las hace
  estornudar) y, si uno de los dos deja de reírse de verdad, la mascota se
  vuelve transparente y desaparece
- **Detalle sembrado**: Soup, la primera mascota, apareció "on the worst day of
  my life" (bloque 3), y "a fake laugh makes them sneeze" (bloque 2). En el
  bloque 7, la mascota nueva nace otra vez del peor día, cuando los dos lloran
  y se ríen de lo mal que suenan
- **Giro**: el narrador confiesa que ya no se ríe porque le dé risa, sino por
  miedo a que desaparezcan; su amigo confiesa lo mismo. Soup se va de todas
  formas. Lo que salva la amistad no es conservar los chistes viejos sino
  hacer uno nuevo, y sale de la tristeza compartida
- **Conteo real**: 379 palabras (20, 69, 51, 38, 75, 47, 58, 21), contadas con script
- **Título alterno**: Long Distance

## Narración

El texto de la narración va en inglés, a ras de margen, listo para pegar en el
generador de voz. También está en `006-inside-jokes-become-pets.txt`.

**[1. Gancho]**

In this town, every inside joke turns into a PET, and it lives as long as you both keep laughing.

**[2. Ejemplos del mundo]**

My parents have a tortoise from a joke about a waiter in 1999. Nobody remembers the joke. They just point at the tortoise and wheeze. The twins next door have fifty-two hamsters. My principal has zero pets and a very clean office. You can't fake it, either. A fake laugh makes them sneeze. And when one of you stops laughing for real, the pet goes SEE-THROUGH. Then it's gone.

**[3. El ángulo del narrador]**

Me and Ozzie had fourteen. The first one was Soup. Soup is a duck who wears one sock. He showed up on the worst day of my life. I dropped my lunch tray in front of the whole cafeteria. Ozzie looked at me. Then he dropped his on purpose. Boom. DUCK.

**[4. Crisis]**

Then Ozzie's mom got a job nine hundred miles away. He moved in August. By October we were down to SIX. The llama went see-through in the middle of my math test. Turns out jokes don't TRAVEL well.

**[5. Tres intentos fallidos]**

So I tried to save them. First, video calls. We laughed on a two-second delay. The hedgehog flickered like bad wifi and blinked out. Second, I mailed him forty-one pages of our best jokes. It took six days. By then the iguana was just a tail. Third, I recorded us laughing and played it for Soup all night on a loop. Soup sneezed two hundred times. By morning I could see my carpet through him.

**[6. Cuarto intento]**

Soup was the last one. So I called Ozzie, and I stopped doing bits. "I'm not laughing because it's funny anymore. I'm laughing so they don't disappear. If Soup goes, I think we go too." Ozzie was quiet. Then he said, "I've been FAKE laughing since Halloween."

**[7. Desenlace]**

Soup quacked once and faded out. Only the sock stayed. We both cried, on a two-second delay, so we had to take turns. Ozzie said we sounded like two broken tea kettles. And we lost it. REAL laughing. The can't-breathe kind. Something landed on my desk. A small, soggy pigeon with a face like it had been crying.

**[8. Remate]**

We named him Long Distance. He sleeps on Soup's sock. He only eats when Ozzie calls. He is getting EXTREMELY fat.

# Guion 007: In This World, Everyone Can See Who You Miss

Guion original. Sale de la premisa 11 del banco
(`docs/05-guiones-y-fuentes.md`): la silueta de quien extrañas camina a tu
lado. Aquí la silueta que delata al narrador es la de su peor enemigo.

- **Tema**: amistad disfrazada de rivalidad
- **Final**: cómico con un golpe tierno antes del remate
- **Regla**: la silueta de la persona que extrañas camina a tu lado, gris y
  transparente como niebla, y todos la ven
- **Costo de la regla**: no se puede disimular; entre más extrañas, más nítida
  se pone, y solo se va cuando vuelves a ver a la persona en vivo
- **Detalle sembrado**: "some guy in a fake mustache keeps booing me from the
  back row. Unrelated." (bloque 3). En el bloque 7, Barty no tiene silueta
  porque nunca dejó de ver al narrador: él era el del bigote
- **Giro**: el narrador admite que extraña a su enemigo y descubre que al lado
  de Barty no hay nadie. No es porque no lo extrañe: es porque recorrió seis
  millas cada semana, disfrazado, para no tener que extrañarlo
- **Conteo real**: 396 palabras (17, 70, 64, 35, 84, 45, 56, 25), contadas con script
- **Título alterno**: Foggy Barty

## Narración

El texto de la narración va en inglés, a ras de margen, listo para pegar en el
generador de voz. También está en `007-everyone-can-see-who-you-miss.txt`.

**[1. Gancho]**

In this world, everyone can see who you MISS, because their silhouette walks right next to you.

**[2. Ejemplos del mundo]**

It's gray and see-through, like a person made of fog. My mom's is shaped like my grandma. My gym teacher's is shaped like his own hair in 2009. The more you miss somebody, the sharper it gets. It only goes away when you see them again, in person. So nobody gets to play it cool. My sister told everyone she was "so over" Kyle. Kyle's fog was carrying her backpack.

**[3. El ángulo del narrador]**

Mine is shaped like Barty Finch. My biggest RIVAL. Three years of war. Spelling bees. One corn-eating contest that sent us both to the nurse. Then he transferred to a school six miles away. Now I win everything. Last week I won the spelling bee with the word "cat." Also, some guy in a fake mustache keeps booing me from the back row. Unrelated.

**[4. Crisis]**

Two days after he left, foggy Barty showed up beside me. Everyone saw. And yearbook photos are Friday. I am not getting photographed next to my rival. He's getting sharper, too. He has EYEBROWS now.

**[5. Tres intentos fallidos]**

So I tried to get rid of him. First, I tried missing someone else harder. I stared at pictures of my grandma for two hours. Now I had TWO fogs. They high-fived. Second, I put a wig on him and said he was my cousin. The wig fell straight through. Third, I held auditions for a new rival. Seven kids showed up. The best one lost on purpose and said "good game." DISGUSTING. Foggy Barty got so sharp I could count his freckles. Eleven.

**[6. Cuarto intento]**

So Thursday I biked six miles to his school. I waited at the gate. When he came out, I just said it. "I win everything now, and it feels like nothing. Nobody else argues right. I MISS you, okay?" My fog POPPED like a bubble.

**[7. Desenlace]**

Then I noticed. There was nothing next to Barty. NO fog. My stomach dropped. He turned red. He reached into his backpack and pulled out a fake mustache. "You can't miss somebody you see every week," he said. "Also, your spelling is embarrassing." He'd come to every contest. Six miles each way. Just to BOO me.

**[8. Remate]**

He transferred back on Monday. We're tied, two hundred twelve to two hundred twelve. Nobody walks next to me anymore. Except Barty. He still boos.

# Guion 008: In This World, You Can Lend Your Courage

Guion original. Sale de la premisa 12 del banco (`docs/05-guiones-y-fuentes.md`):
prestas tu valentía a un amigo y quedas sin ella hasta que la devuelva. Antes de
producirlo, repite la búsqueda del título en YouTube y reescribe a tu gusto el
gancho y el remate (hay alternativas al final).

- **Tema**: amistad
- **Final**: emotivo con remate cómico
- **Regla**: la valentía se puede prestar; sale del pecho como una canica
  naranja tibia y el amigo se la pone en el pecho
- **Costo de la regla**: quien la presta queda sin nada de valentía hasta que se
  la devuelvan, y pedirla de vuelta exige justamente valentía
- **Detalle sembrado**: Bram la guarda en el bolsillo de la camisa y lo abotona
  dos veces (bloque 3). Se cosecha en el bloque 7 (sigue ahí, sin usar: nunca se
  la puso) y en el remate (la sigue pidiendo solo para abotonarla)
- **Giro**: Bram cantó muerto de miedo, sin usarla; la guardó porque era como
  tener a su amigo en el escenario. Y el narrador acaba de cruzar la cafetería
  sin una gota de valentía
- **Conteo real**: 397 palabras (20, 60, 49, 44, 81, 42, 63, 38), contadas con script
- **Título alterno**: The Orange Marble

## Narración

El texto de la narración va en inglés, a ras de margen, listo para pegar en el
generador de voz. También está en `008-you-can-lend-your-courage.txt`.

**[1. Gancho]**

In this world, you can LEND your courage to a friend, but you have NONE until they give it back.

**[2. Ejemplos del mundo]**

It pops out of your chest like a warm orange marble. Your friend presses it to their chest, and it sinks right in. Now they're brave, and you're not. My dad lent his to my uncle for a wedding toast. Dad spent the whole party in the coat closet. Kids at my school rent theirs out. Two dollars a recess.

**[3. El ángulo del narrador]**

I never lent mine. Then my best friend Bram had to sing at the talent show. Bram is scared of dogs, escalators, and the word "volunteer." So I handed mine over. He dropped it in his shirt pocket and buttoned it. TWICE. He sang. He got a standing ovation.

**[4. Crisis]**

That was three weeks ago. He never gave it back. Now Bram eats at the loud table by the window, and I'm scared of everything. Stairs. Soup. SOUP is hot, and it moves. And here's the problem. Asking for your courage back takes COURAGE.

**[5. Tres intentos fallidos]**

So I wrote him a note. Four drafts. Then I got scared of his locker and ate it. I paid my little sister five dollars to ask for me. She asked for his pudding instead. She got it. Then I rented courage from a first grader named Zeb. Two dollars. It was the size of a pea. It was exactly enough to pet one goose. The goose bit me. Zeb cried until I gave it back. He kept the two dollars.

**[6. Cuarto intento]**

On Friday I walked to Bram's table with NOTHING. My knees knocked so loud that people turned around. I said, "I need it back. I'm scared of stairs. I'm scared of soup. And I'm scared you like this table better than me."

**[7. Desenlace]**

Bram unbuttoned his pocket. Twice. There it was. Still warm. He never USED it. "I was too scared to put it in," he said. "What if I broke it? So I just sang SCARED." Then why keep it? His ears went red. "It felt like you were up there with me." He looked at my knees. "Wait. You walked over here WITHOUT it?"

**[8. Remate]**

I pressed it back in. Stairs are just stairs again. Bram still borrows it every Friday. He never uses it. He just buttons it twice. And my uncle never returned Dad's. We slide pizza under the closet door.

# Guion 009: In This Town, Apologies Are Paid in Memories

Guion original. Sale de la premisa 13 del banco (`docs/05-guiones-y-fuentes.md`):
pedir perdón cuesta un recuerdo feliz; entre más grave, más valioso. Antes de
producirlo, repite la búsqueda del título en YouTube y reescribe a tu gusto el
gancho y el remate (hay alternativas al final).

- **Tema**: familia (hermanos)
- **Final**: agridulce con remate cómico
- **Regla**: decir "sorry" de verdad cuesta un recuerdo feliz, que sale por la
  oreja como una foto luminosa y vuela hacia la persona herida, que se queda
  con él
- **Costo de la regla**: entre peor la falta, mejor el recuerdo que se pierde;
  el pueblo cobra el precio justo y no se puede pagar con sustitutos
- **Detalle sembrado**: el mejor recuerdo del narrador, la noche del apagón con
  el fuerte de cobijas y una sola cuchara (bloque 3). Se cosecha en el bloque 7:
  es justo el recuerdo que se va, y todo lo que el narrador contó de esa noche
  lo sabe porque su hermana se lo contó después
- **Giro**: el narrador ya no recuerda su mejor noche; su hermana ahora la
  recuerda dos veces, una como ella y otra como él, y así descubre cuánto la
  admiraba
- **Conteo real**: 363 palabras (20, 59, 51, 27, 69, 38, 57, 42), contadas con script
- **Título alterno**: The Blanket Fort

## Narración

El texto de la narración va en inglés, a ras de margen, listo para pegar en el
generador de voz. También está en `009-apologies-are-paid-in-memories.txt`.

**[1. Gancho]**

In this town, saying sorry costs you one happy MEMORY, and the worse you messed up, the better the memory.

**[2. Ejemplos del mundo]**

It slides out of your ear like a little glowing photo and flies to the person you hurt. They keep it. Bump someone in the hall, and you lose a pretty good sandwich. My dad backed over Mr. Tuttle's mailbox and lost a whole BEACH TRIP. Now Mr. Tuttle remembers our vacation. He says the hotel was just okay.

**[3. El ángulo del narrador]**

I'm fourteen, and I've NEVER said sorry. Not once. So I still have every happy memory I ever made. My best one is a blackout when I was seven. Me and my big sister Nell built a blanket fort. We ate a whole tub of melting ice cream with one spoon.

**[4. Crisis]**

Then Nell started packing for college. I said, "Good. I finally get your room." She hasn't spoken to me in nine days. She leaves Sunday at noon.

**[5. Tres intentos fallidos]**

So I tried to fix it for free. I said "my bad." "My bad" costs NOTHING. It bounced off her door. I baked her twenty-four apology cookies. I wrote "oops" on every one in frosting. She fed them to the dog. Then I paid our neighbor Gus six dollars to say sorry for me. He lost a memory of a waterslide. Nell felt nothing. Gus wants his waterslide back.

**[6. Cuarto intento]**

Sunday, 11:52. Her car was packed. I stood in the driveway and said it. "I'm SORRY. I don't want your room. I want YOU in it." My ear got warm. I figured I'd lose my laser tag birthday.

**[7. Desenlace]**

A little photo slid out. I saw a flashlight. A blanket. ONE spoon. Then it flew into Nell's forehead, and I couldn't tell you what was on it. Nell started crying. She hugged me so hard my shoes left the driveway. I don't REMEMBER that blackout anymore. Everything I told you about the fort, Nell told me.

**[8. Remate]**

She got my copy. So now she remembers that night TWICE. Once as her. Once as me. She says in my version, she's ten feet tall. She also says I promised her my dessert until I'm thirty. I can't prove I didn't.

2	# Guion 010: In This World, Your Best Friend Is Chosen by Lottery
3	
4	Guion original. Sale de la premisa 14 del banco (`docs/05-guiones-y-fuentes.md`):
5	a los diez años un sorteo te asigna un mejor amigo, y al narrador le tocó su
6	peor enemigo. Antes de producirlo, repite la búsqueda del título en YouTube y
7	reescribe a tu gusto el gancho y el remate (hay alternativas al final).
8	
9	- **Tema**: amistad (enemigas)
10	- **Final**: cómico, con un momento tierno antes del remate
11	- **Regla**: al cumplir diez años una máquina de sorteo te asigna a tu mejor
12	  amigo, y es obligatorio por ley
13	- **Costo de la regla**: por ley hay que pasar juntos todos los sábados de dos a
14	  cuatro; la única salida es que un inspector, a los catorce, los declare "no
15	  compatibles"
16	- **Detalle sembrado**: en segundo grado Birdie le contó a todo el salón que la
17	  narradora se comió un crayón verde (bloque 3). Se cosecha en el bloque 7
18	  (Birdie se había comido primero el azul y la delató por miedo) y en la última
19	  frase
20	- **Giro**: la narradora no logra decir "no la quiero" porque el sábado a las
21	  dos es el único momento de la semana en que alguien la espera; y la enemiga
22	  lleva seis años con el remordimiento del crayón
23	- **Conteo real**: 373 palabras (20, 60, 56, 37, 69, 46, 52, 33), contadas con script
24	- **Título alterno**: The Green Crayon

26	## Narración
27	
28	El texto de la narración va en inglés, a ras de margen, listo para pegar en el
29	generador de voz. También está en `010-your-best-friend-is-chosen-by-lottery.txt`.
30	
31	**[1. Gancho]**
32	
33	In this world, a LOTTERY picks your best friend when you turn ten, and you're stuck with them by LAW.
34	
35	**[2. Ejemplos del mundo]**
36	
37	There's a gold machine at Town Hall full of ping-pong balls. One pops out with a name on it. That's your person. My brother got a kid with a trampoline. My cousin got a boy who lives across the ocean. They've been best friends for six years. Neither one speaks the other's language. They mail each other drawings of dogs.
38	
39	**[3. El ángulo del narrador]**
40	
41	My ball said Birdie Vance. My WORST ENEMY. In second grade, she told the whole class I ate a crayon. A green one. I did. But still. By law, best friends spend every Saturday together, two to four. So for four years, we've sat on opposite ends of one park bench. That's 208 Saturdays. ZERO words.
42	
43	**[4. Crisis]**
44	
45	There's one way out. At fourteen, an inspector tests you. If he rules you "not compatible," you both get a new ball. Our inspection was Friday. For the first time ever, Birdie and I agreed on something.
46	
47	**[5. Tres intentos fallidos]**
48	
49	Inspector Plimpton had a clipboard and a very small mustache. First, we argued about pizza toppings for nine minutes. He wrote "passionate." Then Birdie threw my shoe onto the roof. I threw hers. He wrote "shared hobbies." So we staged a giant fight in the cafeteria. We'd rehearsed it all week at my house. We had cue cards. Plimpton wiped his eyes. He wrote, "They finish each other's insults."
50	
51	**[6. Cuarto intento]**
52	
53	"Last chance," he said. "One of you just has to say it. 'I don't want her.'" Easy. I opened my mouth. NOTHING came out. Because Saturday at two is the only time all week somebody is waiting for me. Even if she's waiting to ignore me.
54	
55	**[7. Desenlace]**
56	
57	Birdie stared at her one shoe. Then she said, "I ate the BLUE one." What? "Second grade. I ate a blue crayon first. You saw me. I thought you'd tell. So I told on you." Her chin was shaking. She'd felt sick about it for six years. Plimpton stamped our file. COMPATIBLE.
58	
59	**[8. Remate]**
60	
61	Birdie is still my worst enemy. She's also my best friend. The lottery says that's not a category. Last Saturday we finally talked. Two hours. Mostly about which crayon tastes worse. Green. Obviously.

131	#### FILE 011-parents-can-pause-their-kids.md
132	# Guion 011: In This World, Parents Can Pause Their Kids
133	
134	Guion original. Sale de la premisa 15 del banco (`docs/05-guiones-y-fuentes.md`):
135	cada papá tiene un número de pausas; la mamá del narrador nunca usó ninguna.
136	Antes de producirlo, repite la búsqueda del título en YouTube y reescribe a tu
137	gusto el gancho y el remate (hay alternativas al final).
138	
139	- **Tema**: familia (mamá e hijo)
140	- **Final**: emotivo con remate cómico
141	- **Regla**: cada papá o mamá recibe diez pausas; un clic congela al hijo cinco
142	  minutos y el hijo no siente nada
143	- **Costo de la regla**: son solo diez, no se recuperan y se vencen el día en
144	  que el hijo cumple catorce
145	- **Detalle sembrado**: "I figured I was just an easy kid" y la mamá que se
146	  queda dormida de pie (bloque 3). Se cosecha en el bloque 7: nunca fue un niño
147	  fácil, ella no quería perderse ni cinco minutos de él; y cuando por fin se
148	  duerme, lo hace sobre su hombro
149	- **Giro**: el narrador le ruega a la mamá que lo pause para que ella descanse;
150	  ella no lo hace, las pausas se vencen, y es él quien se queda quieto dos horas
151	  y diez minutos para no despertarla: se pausa solo
152	- **Conteo real**: 369 palabras (18, 58, 69, 47, 52, 33, 71, 21), contadas con script
153	- **Título alterno**: The Clicker
154	
155	Nota de tono: el cansancio de la mamá se muestra con ternura y humor (dormida
156	con una espátula en la mano), nunca como abandono ni como peligro.
157	
158	## Narración
159	
160	El texto de la narración va en inglés, a ras de margen, listo para pegar en el
161	generador de voz. También está en `011-parents-can-pause-their-kids.txt`.
162	
163	**[1. Gancho]**
164	
165	In this world, every parent gets TEN pauses, and one click FREEZES their kid for five whole minutes.
166	
167	**[2. Ejemplos del mundo]**
168	
169	The kid doesn't feel a thing. You blink, and the clock jumped. Mr. Abernathy paused his twins in the middle of a pillow fight. They hung in the air like laundry. My friend Lupe's dad used all ten on one road trip. Lupe says it was the shortest drive of her life. And once they're gone, they're gone.
170	
171	**[3. El ángulo del narrador]**
172	
173	My mom had all ten. She NEVER used one. Not when I painted the dog green. Not when I flooded the bathroom to make a lake. Her clicker is still in the plastic, on her keys. I figured I was just an easy kid. Mom works at the diner all morning and the hospital laundry all night. She falls asleep standing up. Once she did it holding a spatula.
174	
175	**[4. Crisis]**
176	
177	Pauses expire the day you turn fourteen. My birthday was Saturday. And a pause is the only break a parent ever gets. On Monday, Mom fell asleep in the middle of saying my name. So I made a plan. I'd be so annoying she'd have to click.
178	
179	**[5. Tres intentos fallidos]**
180	
181	I played the recorder at six a.m. One song. Forty minutes. She hummed along. I filled the kitchen with two hundred balloons. She popped one, laughed, and made eggs. Then I invited my whole class to dinner without asking. Twenty-six kids. She made twenty-six grilled cheeses. There wasn't one left for her.
182	
183	**[6. Cuarto intento]**
184	
185	Friday night, 11:40, she came home. I tore the plastic off the clicker and put it in her hand. "PAUSE me," I said. "Please. Sit down for five minutes. I won't even know."
186	
187	**[7. Desenlace]**
188	
189	She laughed. Then her eyes got wet. "You think I'm tired because of you? You were NEVER easy. You're the only part of the day I'm AWAKE for." She sat down next to me. At midnight, the clicker went DARK. Mom fell asleep on my shoulder halfway through "happy birthday." So I didn't move. Not for my leg cramp. Not for the itch on my nose. Two hours and ten minutes.
190	
191	**[8. Remate]**
192	
193	Turns out I can pause MYSELF. I'm fourteen now. Nobody can freeze me. And my left arm still hasn't forgiven me.

261	# Guion 012: In This World, You Inherit Your Parents' Fears
262	
263	Guion original. Sale de la premisa 17 del banco (`docs/05-guiones-y-fuentes.md`):
264	al cumplir trece recibes el mayor miedo de tu papá. Antes de producirlo, repite
265	la búsqueda del título en YouTube y reescribe a tu gusto el gancho y el remate
266	(hay alternativas al final).
267	
268	- **Tema**: familia (papá e hijo)
269	- **Final**: cómico, con un momento tierno antes del remate
270	- **Regla**: a la medianoche de tu cumpleaños número trece heredas el mayor
271	  miedo de tu papá, y él lo pierde
272	- **Costo de la regla**: el miedo heredado no se puede devolver
273	- **Detalle sembrado**: el mensaje "Home?" que el papá manda todos los días a
274	  las 3:15 y al que el narrador siempre responde "yep" (bloque 3). Se cosecha en
275	  el bloque 7 (no era una manía: era el miedo, y ese "yep" era la mejor parte
276	  del día del papá) y en el remate (ahora los dos se lo mandan)
277	- **Giro**: el mayor miedo del papá bombero nunca fue el fuego, sino que le
278	  pasara algo a la persona que más quiere. Heredado por el hijo, el miedo apunta
279	  al papá. Y al papá le volvió a crecer al minuto: revisó el cuarto del hijo a
280	  las 12:01
281	- **Conteo real**: 367 palabras (18, 59, 49, 51, 78, 26, 50, 36), contadas con script
282	- **Título alterno**: The 3:15 Text
283	
284	Nota de tono: el oficio de bombero se muestra sin incendios en pantalla. La
285	única emergencia que se ve es un gato en un árbol. El granero es "smoky", con
286	humo y sin llamas.
287	
288	## Narración
289	
290	El texto de la narración va en inglés, a ras de margen, listo para pegar en el
291	generador de voz. También está en `012-you-inherit-your-parents-fears.txt`.
292	
293	**[1. Gancho]**
294	
295	In this world, on your thirteenth birthday, you inherit your dad's biggest FEAR, and he loses it FOREVER.
296	
297	**[2. Ejemplos del mundo]**
298	
299	It hits at midnight like a cold hiccup. My friend Odette got her dad's fear of moths. Now he keeps forty of them in the garage. He named them all. Mr. Park passed down his fear of heights and bought a hot air balloon by breakfast. His son can't use the top bunk. And you can't give it BACK.
300	
301	**[3. El ángulo del narrador]**
302	
303	I wasn't worried. My dad is a firefighter. He once carried a full-grown pony out of a smoky barn. He catches wasps with his bare hand. The only weird thing about Dad is a text. Every day at 3:15, he sends me one word. "HOME?" I always answer "yep."
304	
305	**[4. Crisis]**
306	
307	Midnight. Cold hiccup. I felt nothing. Then Dad grabbed his helmet for the night shift, and my knees turned to PUDDING. His biggest fear was never FIRE. It was something happening to the person he loves most. Now it was mine. And the person I love most rides a fire truck.
308	
309	**[5. Tres intentos fallidos]**
310	
311	So I tried to keep him safe. I texted him "home?" forty-six times in one shift. He wrote back, "At work, bud." Not helpful. I hid his car keys in the freezer. He jogged to the station. Four miles. Then I chased the fire truck on my bike, wearing a snorkel. The emergency was a cat in a tree. I climbed up to help. I got stuck. Dad had to rescue me. The cat walked down by itself.
312	
313	**[6. Cuarto intento]**
314	
315	Halfway down the ladder, over his shoulder, I said it. "I'm SCARED all the time now. Every siren. How did you do this for thirteen years?"
316	
317	**[7. Desenlace]**
318	
319	"BADLY," Dad said. "I texted you every day at 3:15." He set me on the grass. "You'd say 'yep.' Best part of my day." So now he was free, right? He laughed. "It was supposed to leave at midnight. I checked your room at 12:01. I think it GREW back."
320	
321	**[8. Remate]**
322	
323	So now we both have it. At 3:15, I text him "home?" He texts me "home?" We both say "yep." Odette got moths. Honestly? Lucky. Someday my kid gets this one. Sorry, kid. Answer your texts.

393	# Guion 013: In This World, Hugs Are Counted
394	
395	Guion original. Sale de la premisa 18 del banco (`docs/05-guiones-y-fuentes.md`):
396	naces con un número fijo de abrazos, y la abuela guardó los suyos. Antes de
397	producirlo, repite la búsqueda del título en YouTube y reescribe a tu gusto el
398	gancho y el remate (hay alternativas al final).
399	
400	- **Tema**: familia (abuela y nieto)
401	- **Final**: emotivo con remate cómico
402	- **Regla**: cada persona nace con mil abrazos exactos y un contador en la
403	  muñeca que baja con cada uno
404	- **Costo de la regla**: cuando llegas a cero no hay más; y solo paga quien abre
405	  los brazos primero (si los dos los abren al tiempo, pagan los dos). El costo
406	  se dice en la segunda frase del bloque 2 y se muestra con la reunión familiar
407	- **Detalle sembrado**: los once abrazos gastados en un muñeco de nieve llamado
408	  Gerald y la abuela que nunca abre los brazos (bloque 3). Se cosecha en el
409	  bloque 7 (la abuela no era fría: ahorraba, y supo para quién al verlo abrazar
410	  al muñeco once veces) y en el remate
411	- **Giro**: el narrador decide gastar su último abrazo en la abuela; ella lo
412	  detiene y abre los brazos primero, así que paga ella. En 81 años nunca fue
413	  la primera: los estaba guardando sin saber para quién
414	- **Conteo real**: 380 palabras (17, 65, 61, 33, 50, 40, 83, 31), contadas con script
415	- **Título alterno**: The Last Hug

417	Nota de tono: la pérdida solo se sugiere ("Her number drops every day", "Neither of
418	us looks at it"). No se muestra enfermedad ni despedida. La abuela termina la
419	historia viva, abrazando.

421	## Narración
422	
423	El texto de la narración va en inglés, a ras de margen, listo para pegar en el
424	generador de voz. También está en `013-hugs-are-counted.txt`.
425	
426	**[1. Gancho]**
427	
428	In this world, you're born with exactly one THOUSAND hugs, and there's a counter on your wrist.
429	
430	**[2. Ejemplos del mundo]**
431	
432	Every hug, it ticks down. But only for whoever opens their arms FIRST. So nobody goes first. My teacher only gives thumbs-ups. At our family reunion, forty people stood around with their arms down for six hours. My uncle cracked at his own wedding. He hit ZERO before the cake. Now he does finger guns. Dogs don't have counters. Nobody knows why. Everybody knows why.
433	
434	**[3. El ángulo del narrador]**
435	
436	I'm a spender. I always go first. When I was five, I used eleven hugs on one snowman. His name was Gerald. I'm fourteen now, and I have FOUR left. My grandma has nine hundred thirty-one. She has never opened her arms. Not once. She just pats your head twice, like she's checking a melon. I figured she didn't like hugs.
437	
438	**[4. Crisis]**
439	
440	Four hugs. For the rest of my life. And Grandma turns eighty-one on Sunday. I wanted to give her one. I also wanted to keep it. So I tried to cheat the counter.
441	
442	**[5. Tres intentos fallidos]**
443	
444	I hugged my mom wearing oven mitts. It counted. THREE. I hugged a tree and waited for it to go first. Trees never go first. TWO. Then my friend Hollis and I counted down and opened at the exact same time. It charged us both. ONE. Hollis is still mad.
445	
446	**[6. Cuarto intento]**
447	
448	On Sunday, I had one hug and one grandma. She sat in her chair with her hands folded. Same as always. I looked at my wrist. Then I decided she was worth it. I walked up and opened my arms.
449	
450	**[7. Desenlace]**
451	
452	She grabbed my wrists. "Put those away," she said. Then she opened hers. WIDE. I'd never seen her do that. Her counter ticked. Nine hundred thirty. Mine still said one. She smelled like peppermint. "Eighty-one years," she said. "I never went first. I was SAVING them. I just didn't know who for. Then I watched a five-year-old hug a snowman eleven times." She's hugged me every morning since. She always goes FIRST. Her number drops every day. Neither of us looks at it.
453	
454	**[8. Remate]**
455	
456	I still have my one. I'm saving it for something huge. Or for Gerald, if it snows. Grandma says that's the dumbest plan she's ever heard. She's knitting him a scarf.

# Guion 010: In This World, Your Best Friend Is Chosen by Lottery

Guion original. Sale de la premisa 14 del banco (`docs/05-guiones-y-fuentes.md`):
a los diez años un sorteo te asigna un mejor amigo, y al narrador le tocó su
peor enemigo. Antes de producirlo, repite la búsqueda del título en YouTube y
reescribe a tu gusto el gancho y el remate (hay alternativas al final).

- **Tema**: amistad (enemigas)
- **Final**: cómico, con un momento tierno antes del remate
- **Regla**: al cumplir diez años una máquina de sorteo te asigna a tu mejor
  amigo, y es obligatorio por ley
- **Costo de la regla**: por ley hay que pasar juntos todos los sábados de dos a
  cuatro; la única salida es que un inspector, a los catorce, los declare "no
  compatibles"
- **Detalle sembrado**: en segundo grado Birdie le contó a todo el salón que la
  narradora se comió un crayón verde (bloque 3). Se cosecha en el bloque 7
  (Birdie se había comido primero el azul y la delató por miedo) y en la última
  frase
- **Giro**: la narradora no logra decir "no la quiero" porque el sábado a las
  dos es el único momento de la semana en que alguien la espera; y la enemiga
  lleva seis años con el remordimiento del crayón
- **Conteo real**: 373 palabras (20, 60, 56, 37, 69, 46, 52, 33), contadas con script
- **Título alterno**: The Green Crayon

## Narración

El texto de la narración va en inglés, a ras de margen, listo para pegar en el
generador de voz. También está en `010-your-best-friend-is-chosen-by-lottery.txt`.

**[1. Gancho]**

In this world, a LOTTERY picks your best friend when you turn ten, and you're stuck with them by LAW.

**[2. Ejemplos del mundo]**

There's a gold machine at Town Hall full of ping-pong balls. One pops out with a name on it. That's your person. My brother got a kid with a trampoline. My cousin got a boy who lives across the ocean. They've been best friends for six years. Neither one speaks the other's language. They mail each other drawings of dogs.

**[3. El ángulo del narrador]**

My ball said Birdie Vance. My WORST ENEMY. In second grade, she told the whole class I ate a crayon. A green one. I did. But still. By law, best friends spend every Saturday together, two to four. So for four years, we've sat on opposite ends of one park bench. That's 208 Saturdays. ZERO words.

**[4. Crisis]**

There's one way out. At fourteen, an inspector tests you. If he rules you "not compatible," you both get a new ball. Our inspection was Friday. For the first time ever, Birdie and I agreed on something.

**[5. Tres intentos fallidos]**

Inspector Plimpton had a clipboard and a very small mustache. First, we argued about pizza toppings for nine minutes. He wrote "passionate." Then Birdie threw my shoe onto the roof. I threw hers. He wrote "shared hobbies." So we staged a giant fight in the cafeteria. We'd rehearsed it all week at my house. We had cue cards. Plimpton wiped his eyes. He wrote, "They finish each other's insults."

**[6. Cuarto intento]**

"Last chance," he said. "One of you just has to say it. 'I don't want her.'" Easy. I opened my mouth. NOTHING came out. Because Saturday at two is the only time all week somebody is waiting for me. Even if she's waiting to ignore me.

**[7. Desenlace]**

Birdie stared at her one shoe. Then she said, "I ate the BLUE one." What? "Second grade. I ate a blue crayon first. You saw me. I thought you'd tell. So I told on you." Her chin was shaking. She'd felt sick about it for six years. Plimpton stamped our file. COMPATIBLE.

**[8. Remate]**

Birdie is still my worst enemy. She's also my best friend. The lottery says that's not a category. Last Saturday we finally talked. Two hours. Mostly about which crayon tastes worse. Green. Obviously.

#### FILE 011-parents-can-pause-their-kids.md
# Guion 011: In This World, Parents Can Pause Their Kids

Guion original. Sale de la premisa 15 del banco (`docs/05-guiones-y-fuentes.md`):
cada papá tiene un número de pausas; la mamá del narrador nunca usó ninguna.
Antes de producirlo, repite la búsqueda del título en YouTube y reescribe a tu
gusto el gancho y el remate (hay alternativas al final).

- **Tema**: familia (mamá e hijo)
- **Final**: emotivo con remate cómico
- **Regla**: cada papá o mamá recibe diez pausas; un clic congela al hijo cinco
  minutos y el hijo no siente nada
- **Costo de la regla**: son solo diez, no se recuperan y se vencen el día en
  que el hijo cumple catorce
- **Detalle sembrado**: "I figured I was just an easy kid" y la mamá que se
  queda dormida de pie (bloque 3). Se cosecha en el bloque 7: nunca fue un niño
  fácil, ella no quería perderse ni cinco minutos de él; y cuando por fin se
  duerme, lo hace sobre su hombro
- **Giro**: el narrador le ruega a la mamá que lo pause para que ella descanse;
  ella no lo hace, las pausas se vencen, y es él quien se queda quieto dos horas
  y diez minutos para no despertarla: se pausa solo
- **Conteo real**: 369 palabras (18, 58, 69, 47, 52, 33, 71, 21), contadas con script
- **Título alterno**: The Clicker

Nota de tono: el cansancio de la mamá se muestra con ternura y humor (dormida
con una espátula en la mano), nunca como abandono ni como peligro.

## Narración

El texto de la narración va en inglés, a ras de margen, listo para pegar en el
generador de voz. También está en `011-parents-can-pause-their-kids.txt`.

**[1. Gancho]**

In this world, every parent gets TEN pauses, and one click FREEZES their kid for five whole minutes.

**[2. Ejemplos del mundo]**

The kid doesn't feel a thing. You blink, and the clock jumped. Mr. Abernathy paused his twins in the middle of a pillow fight. They hung in the air like laundry. My friend Lupe's dad used all ten on one road trip. Lupe says it was the shortest drive of her life. And once they're gone, they're gone.

**[3. El ángulo del narrador]**

My mom had all ten. She NEVER used one. Not when I painted the dog green. Not when I flooded the bathroom to make a lake. Her clicker is still in the plastic, on her keys. I figured I was just an easy kid. Mom works at the diner all morning and the hospital laundry all night. She falls asleep standing up. Once she did it holding a spatula.

**[4. Crisis]**

Pauses expire the day you turn fourteen. My birthday was Saturday. And a pause is the only break a parent ever gets. On Monday, Mom fell asleep in the middle of saying my name. So I made a plan. I'd be so annoying she'd have to click.

**[5. Tres intentos fallidos]**

I played the recorder at six a.m. One song. Forty minutes. She hummed along. I filled the kitchen with two hundred balloons. She popped one, laughed, and made eggs. Then I invited my whole class to dinner without asking. Twenty-six kids. She made twenty-six grilled cheeses. There wasn't one left for her.

**[6. Cuarto intento]**

Friday night, 11:40, she came home. I tore the plastic off the clicker and put it in her hand. "PAUSE me," I said. "Please. Sit down for five minutes. I won't even know."

**[7. Desenlace]**

She laughed. Then her eyes got wet. "You think I'm tired because of you? You were NEVER easy. You're the only part of the day I'm AWAKE for." She sat down next to me. At midnight, the clicker went DARK. Mom fell asleep on my shoulder halfway through "happy birthday." So I didn't move. Not for my leg cramp. Not for the itch on my nose. Two hours and ten minutes.

**[8. Remate]**

Turns out I can pause MYSELF. I'm fourteen now. Nobody can freeze me. And my left arm still hasn't forgiven me.

#### FILE 012-you-inherit-your-parents-fears.md
# Guion 012: In This World, You Inherit Your Parents' Fears

Guion original. Sale de la premisa 17 del banco (`docs/05-guiones-y-fuentes.md`):
al cumplir trece recibes el mayor miedo de tu papá. Antes de producirlo, repite
la búsqueda del título en YouTube y reescribe a tu gusto el gancho y el remate
(hay alternativas al final).

- **Tema**: familia (papá e hijo)
- **Final**: cómico, con un momento tierno antes del remate
- **Regla**: a la medianoche de tu cumpleaños número trece heredas el mayor
  miedo de tu papá, y él lo pierde
- **Costo de la regla**: el miedo heredado no se puede devolver
- **Detalle sembrado**: el mensaje "Home?" que el papá manda todos los días a
  las 3:15 y al que el narrador siempre responde "yep" (bloque 3). Se cosecha en
  el bloque 7 (no era una manía: era el miedo, y ese "yep" era la mejor parte
  del día del papá) y en el remate (ahora los dos se lo mandan)
- **Giro**: el mayor miedo del papá bombero nunca fue el fuego, sino que le
  pasara algo a la persona que más quiere. Heredado por el hijo, el miedo apunta
  al papá. Y al papá le volvió a crecer al minuto: revisó el cuarto del hijo a
  las 12:01
- **Conteo real**: 367 palabras (18, 59, 49, 51, 78, 26, 50, 36), contadas con script
- **Título alterno**: The 3:15 Text

Nota de tono: el oficio de bombero se muestra sin incendios en pantalla. La
única emergencia que se ve es un gato en un árbol. El granero es "smoky", con
humo y sin llamas.

## Narración

El texto de la narración va en inglés, a ras de margen, listo para pegar en el
generador de voz. También está en `012-you-inherit-your-parents-fears.txt`.

**[1. Gancho]**

In this world, on your thirteenth birthday, you inherit your dad's biggest FEAR, and he loses it FOREVER.

**[2. Ejemplos del mundo]**

It hits at midnight like a cold hiccup. My friend Odette got her dad's fear of moths. Now he keeps forty of them in the garage. He named them all. Mr. Park passed down his fear of heights and bought a hot air balloon by breakfast. His son can't use the top bunk. And you can't give it BACK.

**[3. El ángulo del narrador]**

I wasn't worried. My dad is a firefighter. He once carried a full-grown pony out of a smoky barn. He catches wasps with his bare hand. The only weird thing about Dad is a text. Every day at 3:15, he sends me one word. "HOME?" I always answer "yep."

**[4. Crisis]**

Midnight. Cold hiccup. I felt nothing. Then Dad grabbed his helmet for the night shift, and my knees turned to PUDDING. His biggest fear was never FIRE. It was something happening to the person he loves most. Now it was mine. And the person I love most rides a fire truck.

**[5. Tres intentos fallidos]**

So I tried to keep him safe. I texted him "home?" forty-six times in one shift. He wrote back, "At work, bud." Not helpful. I hid his car keys in the freezer. He jogged to the station. Four miles. Then I chased the fire truck on my bike, wearing a snorkel. The emergency was a cat in a tree. I climbed up to help. I got stuck. Dad had to rescue me. The cat walked down by itself.

**[6. Cuarto intento]**

Halfway down the ladder, over his shoulder, I said it. "I'm SCARED all the time now. Every siren. How did you do this for thirteen years?"

**[7. Desenlace]**

"BADLY," Dad said. "I texted you every day at 3:15." He set me on the grass. "You'd say 'yep.' Best part of my day." So now he was free, right? He laughed. "It was supposed to leave at midnight. I checked your room at 12:01. I think it GREW back."

**[8. Remate]**

So now we both have it. At 3:15, I text him "home?" He texts me "home?" We both say "yep." Odette got moths. Honestly? Lucky. Someday my kid gets this one. Sorry, kid. Answer your texts.

#### FILE 013-hugs-are-counted.md
# Guion 013: In This World, Hugs Are Counted

Guion original. Sale de la premisa 18 del banco (`docs/05-guiones-y-fuentes.md`):
naces con un número fijo de abrazos, y la abuela guardó los suyos. Antes de
producirlo, repite la búsqueda del título en YouTube y reescribe a tu gusto el
gancho y el remate (hay alternativas al final).

- **Tema**: familia (abuela y nieto)
- **Final**: emotivo con remate cómico
- **Regla**: cada persona nace con mil abrazos exactos y un contador en la
  muñeca que baja con cada uno
- **Costo de la regla**: cuando llegas a cero no hay más; y solo paga quien abre
  los brazos primero (si los dos los abren al tiempo, pagan los dos). El costo
  se dice en la segunda frase del bloque 2 y se muestra con la reunión familiar
- **Detalle sembrado**: los once abrazos gastados en un muñeco de nieve llamado
  Gerald y la abuela que nunca abre los brazos (bloque 3). Se cosecha en el
  bloque 7 (la abuela no era fría: ahorraba, y supo para quién al verlo abrazar
  al muñeco once veces) y en el remate
- **Giro**: el narrador decide gastar su último abrazo en la abuela; ella lo
  detiene y abre los brazos primero, así que paga ella. En 81 años nunca fue
  la primera: los estaba guardando sin saber para quién
- **Conteo real**: 380 palabras (17, 65, 61, 33, 50, 40, 83, 31), contadas con script
- **Título alterno**: The Last Hug

Nota de tono: la pérdida solo se sugiere ("Her number drops every day", "Neither of
us looks at it"). No se muestra enfermedad ni despedida. La abuela termina la
historia viva, abrazando.

## Narración

El texto de la narración va en inglés, a ras de margen, listo para pegar en el
generador de voz. También está en `013-hugs-are-counted.txt`.

**[1. Gancho]**

In this world, you're born with exactly one THOUSAND hugs, and there's a counter on your wrist.

**[2. Ejemplos del mundo]**

Every hug, it ticks down. But only for whoever opens their arms FIRST. So nobody goes first. My teacher only gives thumbs-ups. At our family reunion, forty people stood around with their arms down for six hours. My uncle cracked at his own wedding. He hit ZERO before the cake. Now he does finger guns. Dogs don't have counters. Nobody knows why. Everybody knows why.

**[3. El ángulo del narrador]**

I'm a spender. I always go first. When I was five, I used eleven hugs on one snowman. His name was Gerald. I'm fourteen now, and I have FOUR left. My grandma has nine hundred thirty-one. She has never opened her arms. Not once. She just pats your head twice, like she's checking a melon. I figured she didn't like hugs.

**[4. Crisis]**

Four hugs. For the rest of my life. And Grandma turns eighty-one on Sunday. I wanted to give her one. I also wanted to keep it. So I tried to cheat the counter.

**[5. Tres intentos fallidos]**

I hugged my mom wearing oven mitts. It counted. THREE. I hugged a tree and waited for it to go first. Trees never go first. TWO. Then my friend Hollis and I counted down and opened at the exact same time. It charged us both. ONE. Hollis is still mad.

**[6. Cuarto intento]**

On Sunday, I had one hug and one grandma. She sat in her chair with her hands folded. Same as always. I looked at my wrist. Then I decided she was worth it. I walked up and opened my arms.

**[7. Desenlace]**

She grabbed my wrists. "Put those away," she said. Then she opened hers. WIDE. I'd never seen her do that. Her counter ticked. Nine hundred thirty. Mine still said one. She smelled like peppermint. "Eighty-one years," she said. "I never went first. I was SAVING them. I just didn't know who for. Then I watched a five-year-old hug a snowman eleven times." She's hugged me every morning since. She always goes FIRST. Her number drops every day. Neither of us looks at it.

**[8. Remate]**

I still have my one. I'm saving it for something huge. Or for Gerald, if it snows. Grandma says that's the dumbest plan she's ever heard. She's knitting him a scarf.

132	# Guion 003: In This World, You Only Get Three "I Love Yous"
133	
134	Guion original. Sale de la premisa 3 del banco
135	(`docs/05-guiones-y-fuentes.md`): cada persona nace con tres, y al narrador le
136	queda una. Aquí la última no se gasta en un romance sino en el papá, que ya no
137	tiene ninguna para responder.
138	
139	- **Tema**: familia (hijo o hija de 14 años y su papá), dentro de la línea de
140	  amor
141	- **Final**: agridulce con remate cómico
142	- **Regla**: cada persona puede decir "I love you" solo tres veces en la vida;
143	  tres lucecitas en la muñeca llevan la cuenta
144	- **Costo de la regla**: al gastar la tercera no se puede volver a decir nunca,
145	  ni por escrito, ni en otro idioma, ni por encargo
146	- **Detalle sembrado**: el papá, que está en cero, pregunta todas las mañanas
147	  "Got your shoes tied?" y al narrador le parece ridículo porque tiene catorce
148	  años (bloque 3); en el bloque 7 esa pregunta resulta ser la forma en que el
149	  papá lo ha dicho unas cinco mil veces
150	- **Giro**: el narrador gasta su última y el papá no puede devolverla; la
151	  respuesta llega en la frase de siempre. El final no es "él también me lo
152	  dijo", es descubrir que ya lo venía diciendo
153	- **Conteo real**: 392 palabras (19, 73, 49, 44, 81, 34, 54, 38), contadas con script
154	- **Título alterno**: Three Lights
155	
156	## Narración
157	
158	El texto de la narración va en inglés, a ras de margen, listo para pegar en el
159	generador de voz. También está en `003-only-three-i-love-yous.txt`.
160	
161	**[1. Gancho]**
162	
163	In this world, you can only say "I love you" THREE times in your whole life. Then NEVER again.
164	
165	**[2. Ejemplos del mundo]**
166	
167	You're born with three little lights on your wrist. Say the words, and one goes dark. My aunt used all three on the same guy. He moved to Alaska. Our neighbor is ninety-one and still has all three. He's waiting for the right moment. My dad has zero. He spent one on my mom. One on me, the day I was born. And one on a chili dog in 1996. He regrets nothing.
168	
169	**[3. El ángulo del narrador]**
170	
171	I have ONE left. I lost my first at age four, to a balloon. I lost my second hanging up on the pizza guy. "Okay, love you, bye." He said, "Thanks?" Dad can't say it at all anymore. Every morning he just asks, "Got your shoes tied?" I'm fourteen.
172	
173	**[4. Crisis]**
174	
175	Then Dad got a job on a research boat. Eleven months at sea. He was leaving Friday on the six a.m. bus. I wanted him to know. But everybody says to save your last one for your wedding. So I looked for a loophole.
176	
177	**[5. Tres intentos fallidos]**
178	
179	First, I wrote it on a card. The ink slid right off the paper and made a puddle on my desk. Second, I tried it in French. My mouth honked like a goose. Third, I rented a parrot named Mr. Biscuit for twelve dollars and taught him the words. He said them perfectly. To my dad. One of the tiny lights on his leg went out. Now Mr. Biscuit was in love with my father, and I was out twelve dollars.
180	
181	**[6. Cuarto intento]**
182	
183	Friday, six a.m. The bus doors opened. Dad picked up his bag. And I stopped caring about my wedding. I grabbed his sleeve and said it. All three words. My last light went DARK.
184	
185	**[7. Desenlace]**
186	
187	Dad opened his mouth. NOTHING came out. He's been empty since the day I was born. His eyes got shiny. Then he looked down at my sneakers. "Got your shoes TIED?" And I finally heard it. He'd asked me that every morning for fourteen years. That's about FIVE THOUSAND times. "Double knots," I said.
188	
189	**[8. Remate]**
190	
191	The bus left. I'm at ZERO now. This morning I asked my little sister if her shoes were tied. She was wearing sandals. She hugged me anyway. Mr. Biscuit still has two left. He's saving them for Dad.

395	# Guion 005: In This Town, Breakups Make It Snow
396	
397	Guion original. Sale de la premisa 6 del banco
398	(`docs/05-guiones-y-fuentes.md`): cada ruptura trae nieve, y lleva tres meses
399	nevando sobre una sola casa. Aquí la casa es la del narrador, y la nieve no es
400	de quien todos creen: el narrador lo sabe desde el principio y lo esconde.
401

298	**[1. Gancho]**
299	
300	In this world, you can LEND your courage to a friend, but you have NONE until they give it back.
301	
302	**[2. Ejemplos del mundo]**
303	
304	It pops out of your chest like a warm orange marble. Your friend presses it to their chest, and it sinks right in. Now they're brave, and you're not. My dad lent his to my uncle for a wedding toast. Dad spent the whole party in the coat closet. Kids at my school rent theirs out. Two dollars a recess.
305	
306	**[3. El ángulo del narrador]**
307	
308	I never lent mine. Then my best friend Bram had to sing at the talent show. Bram is scared of dogs, escalators, and the word "volunteer." So I handed mine over. He dropped it in his shirt pocket and buttoned it. TWICE. He sang. He got a standing ovation.
309	
310	**[4. Crisis]**
311	
312	That was three weeks ago. He never gave it back. Now Bram eats at the loud table by the window, and I'm scared of everything. Stairs. Soup. SOUP is hot, and it moves. And here's the problem. Asking for your courage back takes COURAGE.
313	
314	**[5. Tres intentos fallidos]**
315	
316	So I wrote him a note. Four drafts. Then I got scared of his locker and ate it. I paid my little sister five dollars to ask for me. She asked for his pudding instead. She got it. Then I rented courage from a first grader named Zeb. Two dollars. It was the size of a pea. It was exactly enough to pet one goose. The goose bit me. Zeb cried until I gave it back. He kept the two dollars.
317	
318	**[6. Cuarto intento]**
319	
320	On Friday I walked to Bram's table with NOTHING. My knees knocked so loud that people turned around. I said, "I need it back. I'm scared of stairs. I'm scared of soup. And I'm scared you like this table better than me."
321	
322	**[7. Desenlace]**
323	
324	Bram unbuttoned his pocket. Twice. There it was. Still warm. He never USED it. "I was too scared to put it in," he said. "What if I broke it? So I just sang SCARED." Then why keep it? His ears went red. "It felt like you were up there with me." He looked at my knees. "Wait. You walked over here WITHOUT it?"
325	
326	**[8. Remate]**
327	
328	I pressed it back in. Stairs are just stairs again. Bram still borrows it every Friday. He never uses it. He just buttons it twice. And my uncle never returned Dad's. We slide pizza under the closet door.

2	# Guion 010: In This World, Your Best Friend Is Chosen by Lottery
3	
4	Guion original. Sale de la premisa 14 del banco (`docs/05-guiones-y-fuentes.md`):
5	a los diez años un sorteo te asigna un mejor amigo, y al narrador le tocó su
6	peor enemigo. Antes de producirlo, repite la búsqueda del título en YouTube y
7	reescribe a tu gusto el gancho y el remate (hay alternativas al final).
8	
9	- **Tema**: amistad (enemigas)
10	- **Final**: cómico, con un momento tierno antes del remate
11	- **Regla**: al cumplir diez años una máquina de sorteo te asigna a tu mejor
12	  amigo, y es obligatorio por ley
13	- **Costo de la regla**: por ley hay que pasar juntos todos los sábados de dos a
14	  cuatro; la única salida es que un inspector, a los catorce, los declare "no
15	  compatibles"
16	- **Detalle sembrado**: en segundo grado Birdie le contó a todo el salón que la
17	  narradora se comió un crayón verde (bloque 3). Se cosecha en el bloque 7
18	  (Birdie se había comido primero el azul y la delató por miedo) y en la última
19	  frase
20	- **Giro**: la narradora no logra decir "no la quiero" porque el sábado a las
21	  dos es el único momento de la semana en que alguien la espera; y la enemiga
22	  lleva seis años con el remordimiento del crayón
23	- **Conteo real**: 373 palabras (20, 60, 56, 37, 69, 46, 52, 33), contadas con script
24	- **Título alterno**: The Green Crayon
25	
26	## Narración
27	
28	El texto de la narración va en inglés, a ras de margen, listo para pegar en el
29	generador de voz. También está en `010-your-best-friend-is-chosen-by-lottery.txt`.
30	
31	**[1. Gancho]**
32	
33	In this world, a LOTTERY picks your best friend when you turn ten, and you're stuck with them by LAW.
34	
35	**[2. Ejemplos del mundo]**
36	
37	There's a gold machine at Town Hall full of ping-pong balls. One pops out with a name on it. That's your person. My brother got a kid with a trampoline. My cousin got a boy who lives across the ocean. They've been best friends for six years. Neither one speaks the other's language. They mail each other drawings of dogs.
38	
39	**[3. El ángulo del narrador]**
40	
41	My ball said Birdie Vance. My WORST ENEMY. In second grade, she told the whole class I ate a crayon. A green one. I did. But still. By law, best friends spend every Saturday together, two to four. So for four years, we've sat on opposite ends of one park bench. That's 208 Saturdays. ZERO words.
42	
43	**[4. Crisis]**
44	
45	There's one way out. At fourteen, an inspector tests you. If he rules you "not compatible," you both get a new ball. Our inspection was Friday. For the first time ever, Birdie and I agreed on something.
46	
47	**[5. Tres intentos fallidos]**
48	
49	Inspector Plimpton had a clipboard and a very small mustache. First, we argued about pizza toppings for nine minutes. He wrote "passionate." Then Birdie threw my shoe onto the roof. I threw hers. He wrote "shared hobbies." So we staged a giant fight in the cafeteria. We'd rehearsed it all week at my house. We had cue cards. Plimpton wiped his eyes. He wrote, "They finish each other's insults."
50	
51	**[6. Cuarto intento]**
52	
53	"Last chance," he said. "One of you just has to say it. 'I don't want her.'" Easy. I opened my mouth. NOTHING came out. Because Saturday at two is the only time all week somebody is waiting for me. Even if she's waiting to ignore me.
54	
55	**[7. Desenlace]**
56	
57	Birdie stared at her one shoe. Then she said, "I ate the BLUE one." What? "Second grade. I ate a blue crayon first. You saw me. I thought you'd tell. So I told on you." Her chin was shaking. She'd felt sick about it for six years. Plimpton stamped our file. COMPATIBLE.
58	
59	**[8. Remate]**
60	
61	Birdie is still my worst enemy. She's also my best friend. The lottery says that's not a category. Last Saturday we finally talked. Two hours. Mostly about which crayon tastes worse. Green. Obviously.

131	#### FILE 011-parents-can-pause-their-kids.md
132	# Guion 011: In This World, Parents Can Pause Their Kids
133	
134	Guion original. Sale de la premisa 15 del banco (`docs/05-guiones-y-fuentes.md`):
135	cada papá tiene un número de pausas; la mamá del narrador nunca usó ninguna.
136	Antes de producirlo, repite la búsqueda del título en YouTube y reescribe a tu
137	gusto el gancho y el remate (hay alternativas al final).
138	
139	- **Tema**: familia (mamá e hijo)
140	- **Final**: emotivo con remate cómico
141	- **Regla**: cada papá o mamá recibe diez pausas; un clic congela al hijo cinco
142	  minutos y el hijo no siente nada
143	- **Costo de la regla**: son solo diez, no se recuperan y se vencen el día en
144	  que el hijo cumple catorce
145	- **Detalle sembrado**: "I figured I was just an easy kid" y la mamá que se
146	  queda dormida de pie (bloque 3). Se cosecha en el bloque 7: nunca fue un niño
147	  fácil, ella no quería perderse ni cinco minutos de él; y cuando por fin se
148	  duerme, lo hace sobre su hombro
149	- **Giro**: el narrador le ruega a la mamá que lo pause para que ella descanse;
150	  ella no lo hace, las pausas se vencen, y es él quien se queda quieto dos horas
151	  y diez minutos para no despertarla: se pausa solo
152	- **Conteo real**: 369 palabras (18, 58, 69, 47, 52, 33, 71, 21), contadas con script
153	- **Título alterno**: The Clicker
154	
155	Nota de tono: el cansancio de la mamá se muestra con ternura y humor (dormida
156	con una espátula en la mano), nunca como abandono ni como peligro.
157	
158	## Narración
159	
160	El texto de la narración va en inglés, a ras de margen, listo para pegar en el
161	generador de voz. También está en `011-parents-can-pause-their-kids.txt`.
162	
163	**[1. Gancho]**
164	
165	In this world, every parent gets TEN pauses, and one click FREEZES their kid for five whole minutes.
166	
167	**[2. Ejemplos del mundo]**
168	
169	The kid doesn't feel a thing. You blink, and the clock jumped. Mr. Abernathy paused his twins in the middle of a pillow fight. They hung in the air like laundry. My friend Lupe's dad used all ten on one road trip. Lupe says it was the shortest drive of her life. And once they're gone, they're gone.
170	
171	**[3. El ángulo del narrador]**
172	
173	My mom had all ten. She NEVER used one. Not when I painted the dog green. Not when I flooded the bathroom to make a lake. Her clicker is still in the plastic, on her keys. I figured I was just an easy kid. Mom works at the diner all morning and the hospital laundry all night. She falls asleep standing up. Once she did it holding a spatula.
174	
175	**[4. Crisis]**
176	
177	Pauses expire the day you turn fourteen. My birthday was Saturday. And a pause is the only break a parent ever gets. On Monday, Mom fell asleep in the middle of saying my name. So I made a plan. I'd be so annoying she'd have to click.
178	
179	**[5. Tres intentos fallidos]**
180	
181	I played the recorder at six a.m. One song. Forty minutes. She hummed along. I filled the kitchen with two hundred balloons. She popped one, laughed, and made eggs. Then I invited my whole class to dinner without asking. Twenty-six kids. She made twenty-six grilled cheeses. There wasn't one left for her.
182	
183	**[6. Cuarto intento]**
184	
185	Friday night, 11:40, she came home. I tore the plastic off the clicker and put it in her hand. "PAUSE me," I said. "Please. Sit down for five minutes. I won't even know."
186	
187	**[7. Desenlace]**
188	
189	She laughed. Then her eyes got wet. "You think I'm tired because of you? You were NEVER easy. You're the only part of the day I'm AWAKE for." She sat down next to me. At midnight, the clicker went DARK. Mom fell asleep on my shoulder halfway through "happy birthday." So I didn't move. Not for my leg cramp. Not for the itch on my nose. Two hours and ten minutes.
190	
191	**[8. Remate]**
192	
193	Turns out I can pause MYSELF. I'm fourteen now. Nobody can freeze me. And my left arm still hasn't forgiven me.
